blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how pilots calculate the distance between two cities on the globe?

blocks.markdown: In Earth Geometry, understanding how to calculate distances on the Earth's surface is crucial. This involves using concepts of longitude, latitude, and the Earth's circumference.

blocks.title: Nautical Mile
blocks.text: A nautical mile is a unit of measurement used in air and sea travel, equivalent to one minute of latitude. It is approximately 1,852 meters.

blocks.markdown: To calculate distances on the Earth, we often use nautical miles. Distances along a meridian (longitude) or the equator (latitude) can be calculated using the Earth's circumference.

blocks.title: Calculating Distance Along a Meridian
blocks.prompt: Calculate the distance between two points on the same meridian at latitudes 10°N and 20°N.

steps.text: Convert the latitude difference to nautical miles: $10° \times 60 = 600$ nautical miles.

blocks.markdown: When calculating distances along the equator, the same principle applies, but we consider the Earth's circumference at the equator.

blocks.title: Time Difference Calculation
blocks.text: Remember that 15° of longitude corresponds to a 1-hour time difference. This is useful for calculating time differences between two locations.
